questions.question: Part IV A of the Indian Constitution is related to _________.
questions.solution: Part IV A of the Indian Constitution contains Article 51A, which outlines the Fundamental Duties of its citizens. These were not part of the original Constitution but were added later to emphasize the moral obligations of citizens toward the nation. Note: Part III covers Fundamental Rights, and Part IV covers Directive Principles of State Policy.

questions.question: Which of the following committees had recommended the inclusion of a chapter on the Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India and stressed that the citizens should become conscious that, in addition to the enjoyment of rights, they also have certain duties to perform?
questions.solution: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) was constituted by the government to make recommendations about fundamental duties. The committee stressed that citizens should be conscious that while they enjoy rights, they also have specific duties to perform for the state. This led to the inclusion of the new Chapter IV-A in the Constitution.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution of India deals with ‘Citizenship’?
questions.solution: Part II of the Constitution (Articles 5 to 11) deals with Citizenship. It defines who was considered a citizen of India at the time of the Constitution's commencement and empowers Parliament to enact laws for future citizenship acquisition and termination. Note: Part I deals with the Union and its Territory, and Part III with Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: The 42nd amendment of the Indian Constitution added ________.
questions.solution: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A) to the Constitution. This amendment is often referred to as the 'Mini-Constitution' due to the extensive changes it introduced, including adding 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

questions.question: Who is the author of the Indian national anthem?
questions.solution: Rabindranath Tagore is the author of India's national anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana'. It was originally composed in Bengali. Note: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote 'Vande Mataram', which is the National Song of India.

questions.question: The Constitution of India was adopted on ________.
questions.solution: The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 November 1949 by the Constituent Assembly. This day is celebrated annually as Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas). However, the Constitution came into full effect on 26 January 1950, which we celebrate as Republic Day.

questions.question: From which of the following Constitutions has the India Constitution adopted the system of ‘First Past the Post’?
questions.solution: The 'First Past the Post' (FPTP) system was adopted from the British Constitution. In this voting system, the candidate who receives more votes than any other candidate wins the election, even if they do not receive an absolute majority of the total votes cast.

questions.question: In which year did the Indian Constitution declare Hindi in Devanagari script to be the official language of the Union?
questions.solution: On 14 September 1949, the Constituent Assembly declared Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language of the Union (Article 343). This is why September 14 is celebrated as Hindi Diwas every year in India.

questions.question: Which of the following committees recommended the inclusion of fundamental duties in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution: The Swaran Singh Committee recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties. They argued that if the Constitution provides rights to the people, it should also expect certain duties in return. Note: The Sarkaria Commission dealt with Centre-State relations, and the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee with Panchayati Raj.

questions.question: How many Fundamental Rights were initially provided in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution: Initially, the Constitution of India provided seven Fundamental Rights. These included the Right to Equality, Freedom, against Exploitation, Freedom of Religion, Cultural/Educational Rights, Constitutional Remedies, and the Right to Property. Update: There are currently only six, as the Right to Property was removed.

questions.question: The Preamble of the Constitution describes India as:
questions.solution: The Preamble describes India as a 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic'. Therefore, India is officially a secular state, meaning the state protects all religions equally and does not have an official state religion. Note: The word 'secular' was added in 1976.

questions.question: Judicial Review, a salient feature of the Constitution of India, has been borrowed from which of the following countries?
questions.solution: The concept of Judicial Review was borrowed from the Constitution of the United States (US). It gives the judiciary the power to examine the constitutionality of legislative enactments and executive orders of both the Central and State governments.

questions.question: How many languages are included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India as scheduled languages?
questions.solution: The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution currently includes 22 languages. Initially, there were only 14 languages; others like Sindhi, Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali, Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali were added through later constitutional amendments.

questions.question: Which of the following Fundamental Rights has been deleted from the original list of fundamental rights provided in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution: The Right to Property was deleted from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978. It is no longer a fundamental right but remains a legal/constitutional right under Article 300A.

questions.question: Which of the following word sequences is correct as per the Preamble to the Constitution?
questions.solution: The correct sequence in the Preamble is: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic. This sequence is vital as it defines the nature of the Indian State. Memory Tip: Think of it as 'Triple S, D, R'.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in fundamental duties provided under Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: 'To join Defence forces' is NOT mentioned as a Fundamental Duty. While there is a duty to 'defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so' (Art 51A-d), joining the armed forces is not a mandatory duty for every citizen. Safeguarding public property and respecting the flag are explicitly listed.

questions.question: The Parliament of India has passed the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002, which establishes the basic rights of primary education for children between:
questions.solution: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 established the Right to Education (Article 21A), making it a fundamental right for children between 6 and 14 years to receive free and compulsory education. This amendment also modified Article 45 and added a new Fundamental Duty.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement/(s) is /are true with respect to Supreme Court Observation in A.G. Perarivalan vs The State Of Tamil Nadu State?

1. It highlighted that the Governor’s powers are qualified by the constitutional mandate, chiefly requiring them to act in aid and advice of the council of ministers

2. The bench headed by justice L Nageswara Rao ordered the freedom of one of the convicts in the Rajiv Gandhi assassination case.

3. The bench was of the opinion that there are three sources of power-Governor, Council of Ministers and the Constitution.
questions.solution: Both 1 and 2 are true. In the A.G. Perarivalan case, the SC clarified that the Governor must follow the 'aid and advice' of the Council of Ministers. The Court also used its extraordinary powers under Article 142 to release Perarivalan, noting the long delay by the Governor in deciding on the state's recommendation for his release.

questions.question: The Indian Constitution borrowed the concept of concurrent list from ______________.
questions.solution: The concept of the Concurrent List (where both Centre and States can make laws) was borrowed from the Constitution of Australia. Note: The USSR was the source for Fundamental Duties, and Japan was the source for 'Procedure Established by Law'.

questions.question: The original constitution did NOT mention any fundamental duty because:
questions.option_1: it was expected that the citizens of the country would perform their duties forcefully
questions.option_2: it was expected that the citizens of the country would perform their duties willingly
questions.option_3: initially fundamental duties were punishable as per the constitution
questions.option_4: initially fundamental duties were not expected to be performed
questions.solution: The original Constitution did not include Fundamental Duties because the framers expected that the citizens of the country would perform their duties willingly. They believed that rights and duties are inherently linked and that a responsible citizenry would naturally respect the nation's integrity.

questions.question: Thee 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of Indian Constitution was passed in the year ________.
questions.solution: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act was passed in 1976 during the Emergency. It is the most comprehensive amendment in the history of India, bringing changes to the Preamble, the powers of the Judiciary, and introducing Fundamental Duties.

questions.question: Who has the power to regulate the right of citizenship in India?
questions.solution: The Parliament has the power to regulate the right of citizenship by law under Article 11. This power is absolute and allows Parliament to make any provision with respect to the acquisition and termination of citizenship, overriding any prior constitutional provisions.
